slides.headline:
The scallions go in whole.
The batter is rice, not flour.
slides.subline: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon — a Busan house that has been making the city's own style of scallion pancake for some eighty years, now in the fourth generation of one family

slides.label:
The generation of the same
family running the house in
Dongnae, Busan
slides.note: Busan's official city tourism site describes the restaurant as carrying pajeon through four generations over more than eighty years; the English Wikipedia entry places the founding in the 1940s (some sources say the 1950s) and records the fourth generation as of 2024. Busan's local-culture encyclopedia traces the family further back, to a stall in Dongnae market in the 1930s · current operation, address and phone confirmed against Visit Busan and Korean listing platforms (DiningCode, Siksin, Triple) in September 2026

items.t: Dongnae pajeon, the whole reason to come
items.d: Listed at about 40,000 won for the large and 28,000 won for the small on Korean platforms in September 2026. It is a sharing dish, not a single portion.
Around 30,000 won, and the dish Busan listings name second after the pancake.

items.t: Smaller plates if you want a full table
items.d: Golbaengi-muchim and grilled deodeok root are each listed near 23,000 won, with a barley-rice set around 15,000 and a stone-pot bibimbap around 12,000.

slides.title:
It isn't the
pancake you know
slides.body:
Most pajeon abroad is wheat-flour batter with chopped scallion stirred through it. The Dongnae version is built the other way around.

The scallions stay whole and uncut, laid out in parallel to form a sheet. Seafood goes on top — Busan's own listings name clams, mussels, oysters, shrimp and beef — and only then a small amount of batter, made with glutinous and non-glutinous rice flour rather than wheat, with egg poured over. Closer to a soft, layered thing held at the edges than to a crisp fried disc.

The dish carries a history too. Busan's city materials and its local-culture encyclopedia tie dongnae pajeon to Dongnae's old market and to Joseon-era accounts — made as a substitute meal during work on Geumjeongsanseong fortress, or court technique reaching Dongnae, or sent up to the king by the local magistrate.

Take the origin stories as stories. What is checkable is that the city treats this as its signature hometown dish, and that this house has made it in the same district a long time.

items.d: In Bokcheon-dong, walkable from Dongnae station on Busan Metro Lines 1 and 4. Phone 051-552-0792

items.t: Roughly midday to 21:00, with an afternoon break
items.d: Sources disagree: Visit Busan lists 12:00–15:30 and 17:00–21:00 closed Mondays and Tuesdays, while DiningCode lists 11:30–21:00 with a 15:00–17:00 break and Mondays closed. Call before you travel for it

items.t: Budget for a table, not a plate
items.d: At around 28,000–40,000 won the pancake is priced as something two to four people share, per Korean listings in September 2026. The house also sells a meal-kit version

caption:
Most pajeon is chopped scallion stirred into wheat batter. Busan's Dongnae style leaves the scallions whole and binds them with rice flour and egg.

Dongnae Halmae Pajeon · Bokcheon-dong, Dongnae-gu, Busan · four generations, around eighty years in the same district.

Info as of September 2026; taste is personal.
